package.title: What Happens When You Stop Drinking Alcohol
package.phrase: what happens when you stop drinking alcohol
package.opener: What happens when you stop drinking alcohol? Drinking can disrupt your sleep and stop you sleeping deeply, so cutting down should help you feel more rested when you wake up (NHS). The NHS lists other quick changes: feeling better in the mornings, being less tired during the day, better-looking skin, feeling more energetic and better weight management. If you stop drinking, your liver can often recover (NHS). But if your body is dependent on alcohol, it can be very dangerous to stop suddenly: get medical help before you stop or cut down (NHS). Withdrawal symptoms usually begin within 6 to 12 hours of the last drink (NHS). Call your emergency number (999 in the UK, 911 in the US, 112 in the EU) if someone has severe withdrawal symptoms after stopping, such as visible shaking, confusion, seeing or hearing things that are not there, or a seizure (NHS). If you are worried about your drinking, talk to a doctor or a local alcohol support service.
package.question: Did you know stopping alcohol all at once can be dangerous for some people?

sources.note: 'It can be very dangerous to stop drinking suddenly if you're dependent on alcohol.' 'If you get withdrawal symptoms, get medical help before you try to stop drinking.' 'Withdrawal symptoms begin within 6 to 12 hours of your last drink, and usually last from 3 to 7 days.' Call 999 or go to A&E if someone has severe withdrawal symptoms after stopping drinking alcohol, such as: 'shaking visibly', 'confusion (for example, not knowing what day it is)', 'seeing, hearing, or feeling things that are not there', 'having a seizure'. lines.text: Doc, I stopped. Can my liver heal?
Can I stop all at once?

cta.text: Stopping alcohol? Know this. Your liver can often recover. Drink every day? Don't stop suddenly. Get medical help first. Shaking or confusion? Get emergency help. Follow MedPeak Health for more health tips that keep you safe.
